executive_summary: Five high-signal vulnerabilities were selected from CISA KEV and GitHub Security Advisories spanning Linux kernel security, cloud supply chain, web application secure coding, AI/MCP threat surface, and enterprise identity systems. These items offer direct practical value for portfolio projects, defensive labs, and threat intelligence studies.

signals.title: Linux Kernel TLS receive path improper check for exceptional conditions
signals.what_changed: A zero-length TLS record retrieved from rx_list bypasses recvmsg() record-type handling, causing subsequent records to be processed under incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions.
signals.why_it_matters: Kernel-level TLS processing flaws affect encrypted traffic integrity and can be leveraged for data corruption or privilege escalation in networked systems.
signals.application: Study kernel TLS stack behavior, analyze zero-copy networking assumptions, and build forensic triage scenarios for encrypted traffic anomalies in a lab environment.

signals.title: JFrog Artifactory incorrect authorization via token signature/issuer validation without scope check
signals.what_changed: Token signature and issuer are validated but token scope is not, enabling privilege escalation attacks.
signals.why_it_matters: Supply chain platforms like Artifactory are high-value targets; scope validation gaps allow lateral movement and unauthorized artifact access.
signals.application: Build a mock artifact repository lab to demonstrate token scope validation failures, implement proper scope checks, and create a portfolio project on supply chain security.

signals.title: GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition path traversal in repository commits API
signals.what_changed: Improper path confinement and missing authentication enforcement in the repository commits API allow unauthenticated users to read arbitrary files.
signals.why_it_matters: Path traversal remains a top OWASP vulnerability class; this real-world case demonstrates how missing input validation and auth enforcement combine for critical impact.
signals.application: Construct a controlled vulnerable web app to demonstrate path traversal, then implement path normalization, whitelist validation, and authentication middleware as a secure coding portfolio piece.

signals.title: Obot: Server-Side Request Forgery via remote MCP server URL
signals.what_changed: An SSRF vulnerability exists where a remote MCP server URL can be exploited to induce server-side requests.
signals.why_it_matters: As MCP (Model Context Protocol) adoption grows, AI agent security surfaces expand; SSRF in AI tooling is an emerging threat category requiring defensive research.
signals.application: Set up a local MCP server simulation to study SSRF vectors in AI agent architectures, implement URL allowlisting and egress filtering, and document findings as an AI defense portfolio project.

signals.title: Cisco Identity Services Engine incorrect use of privileged APIs
signals.what_changed: An unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the web-based management interface by exploiting incorrect use of privileged APIs.
signals.why_it_matters: Enterprise identity systems are critical infrastructure; API privilege misuse can lead to full network compromise and unauthorized access control bypass.
signals.application: Study privileged API design patterns, analyze authentication bypass techniques in network devices, and build a network security threat intelligence report as a portfolio deliverable.

experiment.title: Path Traversal Vulnerability Lab: Exploit, Analyze, and Mitigate
experiment.objective: Demonstrate the path traversal vulnerability class (as seen in GitLab CVE-2026-85706) by deploying a controlled vulnerable application, exploiting it to read unauthorized files, then implementing and verifying secure coding mitigations.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of path traversal and input validation
steps: Deploy an intentionally vulnerable Flask application in a Docker container that exposes a file-read endpoint with improper path confinement
Execute path traversal payloads (e.g., ../../etc/passwd) against the endpoint to confirm unauthorized file access
Analyze the vulnerable code to identify missing path normalization and authentication enforcement
Implement fixes: path normalization with os.path.realpath, whitelist-based directory restriction, and authentication middleware
Re-run exploitation attempts to verify all traversal vectors are blocked
Document findings, code diffs, and mitigation verification as a portfolio artifact
expected_evidence: Proof-of-concept output showing unauthorized file read before mitigation
Fixed source code with path normalization and auth enforcement
Test results confirming traversal attempts return 403 or sanitized paths
Written lab report with vulnerability analysis and remediation summary
experiment.stop_condition: All path traversal vectors are blocked, secure coding patterns are verified through automated tests, and the lab report is complete.
